why: The answer applies the documented wrong rule MainWithoutStringArgs: it says public static void main() works as an entry point, but java Hello needs public static void main(String[] args). It compiles, then fails at launch because the main method isn't found.

concepts.quote: main() without String[] args is fine because the program uses no arguments.
concepts.why: This matches the MainWithoutStringArgs error edge: the String[] args parameter is required even when the program reads no arguments.
Saying the program uses no arguments is true of this code, but the answer makes no claim about how command-line arguments work.
The answer says nothing about how java Hello launches or runs the program.
